correctness.rationale: For n>=3, every cycle in K_{2,n} is a 4-cycle involving two complete columns. This gives a union of n PL n-balls sharing an entire boundary Q_n=S^{n-1}, and a relative exact sequence 0->H_n(X;Z)->Z^n->Z->0. The oriented join class transforms by (-1)^{n tau}sgn(sigma), forcing the claimed signed augmentation lattice integrally. Every asserted homotopy or quotient consequence follows from these verified steps. All 1,740 automorphism-character checks for n=3..6 agree; finite checking is supplemental, not proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Theorem 5.5 of Kook–Lee explicitly calculates the S_m × S_k action for a subgroup that fixes one vertex in each bipartition, not the entire graph automorphism group. For K_{2,n}, m=1 and k=n−1, so it determines only S_{n−1}. The root augmentation lattice and the quotient permutation lattice both restrict to isomorphic integral permutation lattices for that subgroup, while differing as full S_n lattices, hence the full integral result does not follow from the stated restricted formula. Kook’s 2006 paper treats coned graphs: a K_{2,n} graph for n>=3 has no universal vertex. The 2020 Alexander-duality correspondence is general but its concrete bipartite calculation is explicitly for the smaller S_m×S_k subgroup, not a full-lattice theorem.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The older bipartite theorem implies rank n−1 and the restriction to S_{n−1}; it does not imply the integral full S2×Sn module. Both Z^n/Z(1,...,1) and ker(sum:Z^n->Z) restrict to Z^{n−1} as permutation modules under S_{n−1}, although they are nonisomorphic as full S_n lattices (the augmentation lattice has H^1(S_n,-)=Z/n). The direct equivariant ball-attachment proof determines which integral extension actually occurs. The quotient rational cohomology is a consequence rather than an independent novelty assertion.

originality.rationale: The 2018 Kook–Lee Theorems 5.3/5.5 already imply the Betti count and the sign-twisted vertex-stabilizer subgroup representation; the new statement explicitly determines the integral full group including interchange of the two degree-n vertices. Moci–Pezzoli Section 6 quotes exactly that subgroup, and general equivariant matroid duality does not supply the special full integral lattice. A systematic comparison of literal implications, aliases and prior historical claims found no covering assertion. Integral root and weight lattices have identical S_{n-1} restrictions, so restricted data do not distinguish this claim.

value.rationale: The forest complex of K_{2,n} is a standard natural infinite family with nonzero cycle-matroid homology. The full integral S2×Sn action is a genuinely stronger invariant than shellability, rank n−1, or Kook–Lee’s fixed-vertex subgroup action. The root vs weight lattice ambiguity shows why integral precision matters; the H1(Sn,A)=Z/n cohomology detects it. The classification works for all n>=3 and gives precise rational quotient consequences, not an arbitrary finite case or a numerical rerun.
